svg.aria-label: How to write દ: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing દ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of દ (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, દ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates દ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper right, circles left and around the rounded upper body, narrows through the middle turn, then continues left and around the broad lower body before rising into the lower-right terminal without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper body, narrow middle turn, broad lower body, and right terminal, but its printed bowls are wider and its terminal more compact than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-body-to-middle-turn-to-lower-body order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the bodies, turn, terminal, and endpoints differently.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
